🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Jerry Koosman, the left-handed pitcher who threw a complete game to clinch the New York Mets' first World Series championship in 1969, has died at 83.

Koosman died on Sunday, November 1, 2026, in Osceola, Wisconsin, after battling multiple illnesses, the Mets announced. He was surrounded by his children.

Born December 23, 1942, in Appleton, Minnesota, Koosman signed with the Mets in 1964 after serving in the U.S. Army at Fort Bragg, North Carolina. He debuted with the club in 1967 and earned back-to-back All-Star selections in 1968 and 1969.

In 1969, he went 17-9 with a 2.28 ERA as the No. 2 starter behind Tom Seaver, helping the once-lowly Mets win 100 games and reach the World Series. Against the heavily favored Baltimore Orioles, he won Game 2 after taking a no-hitter into the seventh inning, then pitched a complete-game five-hitter in Game 5 at Shea Stadium, retiring Davey Johnson on a flyout to left fielder Cleon Jones for the final out of the Mets' first title. Leaping into the arms of catcher Jerry Grote, he became part of one of the most famous images in baseball history.

Koosman also helped the Mets win the National League pennant in 1973. Over 19 major league seasons with the Mets, Minnesota Twins, Chicago White Sox and Philadelphia Phillies, he went 222-209 with a 3.36 ERA and 2,556 strikeouts. The Mets inducted him into their Hall of Fame in 1989 and retired his No. 36 in 2021.

Rest in Peace, Jerry Koosman.

Sources: The Associated Press, via theScore; New York Post; the New York Mets.
